summary: Feed s148_double to IDS is degraded: 24.5% duplicate packets (617/2516) and 100% loss of required VLAN tags (10, 20) - all packets untagged. IDS wastes capacity on duplicates and loses segmentation context for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker aggregating multiple SPAN/mirror or TAP feeds without deduplication, forwarding same packet copies twice. 24.5% duplicates far exceeds 5% threshold (617 of 2516 packets).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU and buffer reprocessing duplicates, inflates flow/event counts, risks state-table exhaustion and TCP reassembly errors, causing missed detections and false positives.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop duplicate copies before IDS ingress and restore 1:1 traffic fidelity.

findings.root_cause: Upstream TAP/SPAN or packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags. Required VLANs 10 and 20 not seen at all; 100% of packets are untagged, indicating tag removal not selective filtering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses VLAN segmentation context for VLANs 10 and 20, cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or detect lateral movement within those segments, effectively blind to those tenants.

recommended_fix.why: Configure SPAN/TAP and packet broker to preserve/pass-through 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10,20 so IDS receives correct segmentation.
